q: The Final Audit authority in India is _____________
e: The correct answer is (D) the Comptroller & Auditor General. Under Articles 148 to 151 of the Constitution, the C&AG is the supreme audit authority of India, auditing the accounts of the Union, the States and bodies like the Railways. Audit is the independent examination of accounts to verify their truth, fairness and compliance with rules and sanctions. q: Audit functions are derived from Articles __________ Constitution of India
e: 148 to 151 — that is the right answer. Article 148 creates the office of the C&AG and protects its independence — appointment by the President, removal only like a Supreme Court judge; Article 149 defines its duties and powers; Articles 150 and 151 deal with the form of accounts and the audit reports laid before Parliament. That is why audit is called a constitutional function. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: Railway Audit was separated from Accounts in the year ________
e: The correct answer is 1929. Railway audit was separated from railway accounts in 1929, giving the C&AG an audit organisation independent of the accounting (PFA) set-up. This independence is the foundation of railway audit: the auditor cannot be subordinate to the authority whose accounts it audits. The scope and extent of railway audit are determined by the C&AG itself. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: Time limit for reply to Draft Para is _________
e: The correct answer is 6 weeks. The railway administration must reply to a Draft Para within six weeks of its issue by the DG/Principal Director of Audit, and the reply must be vetted by the PFA. If audit is not satisfied with the reply, the Draft Para is converted into a Provisional Para, for which the reply window shrinks to 2 weeks. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded. The paper tests exact scope here, not an approximate idea, which is why careful reading of the question stem matters.

q: Time limit for reply to Provisional Para is __________
e: The correct answer is (A) 2 weeks. Once a Draft Para becomes a Provisional Para, the railway administration gets only two weeks to reply — a much tighter window than the six weeks allowed for the Draft Para. q: Reply to Draft Para must be ________ by PFA.
e: The correct answer is Vetted. The reply to a Draft Para must be vetted by the Principal Financial Adviser before it is sent to audit — the PFA checks the facts, figures and the administration's stand. q: If Audit is not satisfied with the reply furnished by Railway administration, the Draft Para converts into ________.
